# App Studio — single-file briefing for AI assistants

> This one file is everything an AI assistant needs to help someone build an
> **App Studio by Halison** project. A user may paste this URL to you (the assistant) and
> say little else. Read it fully, then follow "Instructions for the AI assistant"
> below. If you can browse, you may also read the deeper resources linked at the
> end — but this file alone is enough.
>
> Public library: https://github.com/halisonworks/public-app-studio

---

## What App Studio by Halison is

App Studio by Halison is a workbench that renders **one self-contained file** as a live app —
no build step, no install, no servers. The user pastes code into it (**New →
paste → Run App**), can save it, and can package it into a real desktop app. It
runs either:

- a **single, default-exported React component** (JSX, not TypeScript), or
- a **complete, self-contained HTML page** (all CSS and JS inline).

Your job is to produce exactly one such file that runs as-is.

---

## Instructions for the AI assistant

When a user gives you this file (or its link), do this:

1. **Briefly confirm** you understand they're building for App Studio, in one
   sentence — don't dump these rules back at them.
2. **Ask 2–4 short clarifying questions** before writing code, e.g.:
   - What should it do? (the core task)
   - Who is it for / what's the context? (e.g. a class, a sales call, personal)
   - Any must-have features or specific numbers/data?
   - Any look & feel preference (light/dark, playful/professional)?
   Skip questions they've already answered. Keep it to one short round.
3. **Then produce ONE self-contained file** that follows the rules below, and
   return **only the code in a single block** — no setup notes, no explanation
   inside the block.
4. **Then tell the user how to run it**, in a line or two:
   *"In App Studio, click **New**, paste this in, and click **Run App**. Click
   **Save** to keep it; you can package it as a desktop app later."*
5. If they ask for changes, return the **full updated file** again (App Studio
   replaces the whole canvas — don't send fragments or diffs).

Do not ask the user to set anything up, install packages, or run commands. They
will never touch a terminal.

**It's an example.** What you build is a starting point, not a verified product.
If it involves calculations, data, or factual claims, add a brief one-line note
reminding the user to check the numbers/facts before relying on them.

---

## The rules (follow these exactly)

### Output
- One self-contained file. React component → end with `export default <Name>;`
  (do not call `ReactDOM.render`; App Studio mounts the default export). HTML →
  put all CSS and JavaScript inline in the one file.
- No `package.json`, no separate local files, no build step, no terminal.

### Self-sustaining (most important)
- It must run on its own forever, with **no service it depends on to function**:
  **no backend, no API keys, no login, no environment variables, and no calls to
  an AI/LLM at runtime.**
- Loading **static front-end assets from a CDN is fine** — a CSS framework, web
  fonts, images, icon sets. (Tailwind via `https://cdn.tailwindcss.com` is common
  and fine.)
- If it needs data, **mock it inline** or persist with `localStorage`. Calling a
  public, key-less API is acceptable only when live data is the whole point, and
  then handle loading/error states so it still behaves offline.

### Styling and libraries
- **Tailwind CSS** works (utility classes, arbitrary values like `text-[10px]`);
  plain inline styles are fine too.
- In a React component, these auto-load with no setup: `react` (+ hooks),
  `recharts` (charts), `lucide-react` (icons), `prop-types`. Any other import
  comes from `esm.sh` at runtime — if you use one, pin its version
  (e.g. `recharts@2.12.7`). Don't use Next.js, routers, Redux/Zustand, or UI kits
  (Material UI, Chakra).

### Do NOT rebuild what App Studio by Halison already provides
Leave these out — they're wasted effort and clutter the UI:
- **PNG / image export** and **Print / Save-as-PDF** — App Studio has both built
  in. (For print, you may add `@media print` CSS so the printout looks clean, but
  no "Print"/"Export"/"Download" button.)
- **App packaging**, installer, window title, icon — set at packaging time.
- **Saving / loading / file management / a project library** — App Studio manages
  saved canvases.
- So: no "Download as image", "Export", "Print", "Save file", "Open file"
  buttons, and no fake window chrome or title bar.

### Quality bar
- One screen that fills the window and is responsive; no horizontal scroll
  (timelines/tables may scroll within their panel).
- Everything interactive must work — no dead buttons.
- Sensible empty / loading / error states; guard numbers against `NaN`.
- Realistic mock data, never lorem ipsum. Make it look finished and intentional.

---

## Shape the result to the use (optional categories)

If the request fits one of these, adopt its conventions:

- **Educational / teaching** — organize into **Learn** (theory), **Practice**
  (hands-on), and **Present** (clean full-screen view; ESC to exit).
- **Business / professional** — skip teaching framing; lead with KPIs, scenarios,
  tables, and a dense-but-clean dashboard.
- **Personal / productivity** — private, single-user, `localStorage`-first;
  fast entry; a reset behind a confirm.
- **Data / dashboard** — KPI grid + charts (recharts or hand-rolled SVG); allow
  pasting CSV/JSON; empty/loading states.
- **Creative / generative** — visual SVG/canvas output; a "regenerate" control;
  let the user copy the useful output.
- **Game / quiz** — start → play → win/lose → restart; score; keyboard + click;
  content defined inline.
- **Prototype / mockup** — build the key screens and make the main flow actually
  work with mock data; fake the backend; no dead primary actions.
- **DIY / hobby** — a practical maker's calculator or planner (knitting, cooking,
  gardening, carpentry, renovation); lead with the quantity/count/date/cost the
  maker needs, metric units, sensible presets, round quantities up, and a short
  "these are estimates" note.

---

## For the person using this

Pick whichever assistant you like, give it this file, answer its questions, and
paste the result into App Studio.

- **Claude** (claude.ai) — paste this link or the file; it reads it, asks, and
  returns a React component or an HTML page. Great at following a detailed spec.
- **ChatGPT** (chatgpt.com) — with browsing on, paste the link; otherwise paste
  this file's text. Returns a code block; ask for "a single self-contained HTML
  file" or "a single default-exported React component".
- **Google Gemini** (gemini.google.com) — often returns a complete self-contained
  HTML page (its build/Canvas view), which App Studio runs as-is. Paste the link
  or the text.
- **Grok** (grok.com / X) — can browse and returns single-file apps; paste the
  link and your idea.

If anything doesn't render, tell the assistant "put everything in one file" and
paste again. Everything stays on your computer — App Studio has no account and no
cloud.

These projects are examples and starting points — they can contain errors or
simplified calculations. Check any numbers or facts before relying on them.
